utterances.text: Did you ever receive any information or ever become aware that prisoners, Muslim prisoners, were being held in Bratunac on the night of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did hear, but this is not what I saw. After the funeral, after everything was over and when those civilians or whoever were no longer there, this is when I learned that they had been brought there and that they had been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how many days did you spend in Bratunac in connection with arranging for the funeral of Mr. Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, when we returned from Sandici, the whole day and late into the night, I may even have spent the entire night because it is our custom to sit by the casket. I may have stayed there the entire night, and then the whole day, the next day, until the funeral. So we didn't do anything else. We only were there doing those things connected to the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you receive any orders with respect to your PJP duties, while you were in that area, in terms of where you were supposed to be deployed next?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. There were no orders for our deployment. Later on, after the funeral, the next day, I reported to the police station, I think, to be deployed to my regular duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever become aware that PJP units had been deployed to the area of Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My unit went there. I don't know what date that was. That may have been the day after the funeral. They went to the Baljkovica sector. That's a position near Zvornik. But I did not go there because I was allowed to go to Srebrenica to see my apartment where I had lived before. And that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, sir, do you recall what date it was that your unit was actually deployed to the area of Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it may have been the 15th. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. What I'd like to do now is show you some photographs which you've seen on prior occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: For the record, these are still photographs taken from 65 ter 2047 which can also be found in 65 ter 1936, which is our book of video stills. I believe all the parties have been furnished with my list which identifies these photographs by ERN, chapter and page number of the still book, and time on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you'll see the images popping up on your computer screen momentarily and I'm just going to ask you to see if you can identify some people in them. May we have 4832, please? Do you see an image on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: For the record, this is ERN 0216-4832. Do you see anyone you recognise in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, that's Tomic, Radenko Tomic, if I'm not mistaken, nicknamed Gargija. And seen from the back is our commander, Micic. And I think that here on the left-hand side, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just for some clarification, the individual whom you identified as Mr. Tomic, is he the one to the furthest right of the photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you identify with any more precision the individual you've identified as your platoon commander? Is there anything he's wearing or carrying or anything about his appearance or if you can identify which number he would be moving from right to left in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one next to Tomic, that's him. I know Micic personally, and I'm quite sure that that's him. And I'm right next to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. There is an individual to the left of Mr. Micic who appears to be wearing a helmet and then there is a person to the left of that individual without a helmet. Which individual are you identifying as yourself, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right next to Micic, the person without the helmet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can't we use the gadget or whatever we have?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We'll do that, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It eliminates any doubts in the future. Incidentally, we've got three minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may, Your Honour, I think we have to mark it before the break. So with Madam Usher's assistance -- oh, this is on Sanction? This is being run on Sanction, Your Honour, so unfortunately we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have a still copy of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You mean in hard copy, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, we do. I have them with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have one you can spare that he can mark, then I think we'll most faster and more practical.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we can use the break, Your Honour, to see if there are some other alternatives as well even that might save time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to fill in everybody where we stand on the technology issue, the images on e-court currently are being used through Sanction so we can't mark it with the magic pen. The e-court version unfortunately shows identifying information on the image because it's made from the stills book so we can't use that. So what we will do is display the original photograph on ELMO and I will identify each photograph by ERN. On our exhibit tender list, and I think this also already corresponds with the exhibit list that's been distributed to all parties, we have identified the ERN, the chapter page number and the time on the video so there shouldn't be any ambiguity about the image that we are looking at and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, asking you to look at the photograph which is marked as 0216-4832 on the back. Would you just place the initials RT above the individual you identified as Mr. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would write Mr. Micic's initials above his head, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And your initials above your head, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just place your initials in the upper left-hand corner of the photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we may dispense with placing the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Provided he signs it or puts his initials, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would just place your initials in the upper left-hand corner of the photograph, please, thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you to just pull that away and we'll look at the photograph underneath. Do you see anyone you recognise in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milinkovic, also known as Like, I believe his first name is Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you just place his initials next to him perhaps up near his head where you -- it might be easier to see the initials.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how is it that you know or are familiar with this Mr. Milinkovic, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milinkovic was born and bred in Srebrenica. We lived there together for a part of our childhood. We grew up together.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, same question with respect to Mr. Tomic, whom we just saw a moment ago. How is it that you know him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was in Srebrenica every day. I knew him from before, and I knew him at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd ask you just to remove that photograph and we'll move to the next one, please. You can just pull that right off the stack. Great. Thank you, sir. To save some time, let's just move to the next one and I'm going to ask you a question about the next, if you would, you can remove that photograph and just place it next to you there. There we go. Sir, do you recognise anyone in this photograph, which is 0216-4835?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man in the uniform could possibly be one of our colleagues but I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say, "one of our colleagues," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean a colleague from Vlasenica but I'm not sure. It's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was he a colleague -- if this is the person you're referring to, is this somebody from the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you said, "possibility". How certain or uncertain are you that this is this individual?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 50/50 maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would just flip that photograph over and go to the next photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting but my learned colleague promised us ERN numbers for these photographs. We missed these first two ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought I read that. The photograph of the other individual that we just spoke about is 0216-4835. We are now looking at 0216-4836.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would flip that over, sir? Go to the next photograph. This is 0216-4846. Do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the personal driver of Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin. I think his name was Nedjo. I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. And if you would -- just for the record, this is the individual handing out the candy bar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if you would turn that photograph over and we'll move to the next photograph. This is 0216-4862. Do you recognise anyone in this still, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know them by sight, both of them. I think this one is called Vuksic and the other one, I can't recall at this moment but I know him. I think -- I think his last name is Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you just place a V next to Mr. Vuksic, perhaps in the light-coloured area? Right there, that's perfect, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just an R on the shirt, if you can?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's really not coming out. Might have a dead pen or it may be the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just move along, flip that photograph over, do you recognise anyone in this photograph, sir? This is 0216-4865.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milovanovic -- no, sorry, not Milovanovic. The name eludes me at the moment. Mitrovic, Mitrovic is the last name. I think his first name is Milovan, I'm not sure but I think it's Milovan.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you're placing two Ms above that person?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] I think so. I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how is it that you know or recognise this individual?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was part of the military police, and going about my police business in Bratunac I used to run into this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you said military police. With which brigade or other unit, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just flip that photograph over, sir, and we'll move on to the next one. Do you recognise anyone in this still, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph is a bit blurry, but this than reminds me of a policeman from Skelani who belonged to the Special Police Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know that person's name or nickname, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a nickname, Cop.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this Cop, did this Cop belong to any particular unit of the Special Police Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Special Police Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But within the Special Police Brigade, did he belong to any particular unit or subunit of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was from the Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing I wanted to -- point I wanted to make was the following: This same photo exists on Sanction. I can see it from here. The photo on Sanction is much clearer, much more focused than the photo that the witness is looking at at the moment, and he has sort of pointed or remarked that it is rather blurred. So if we could show him on the screen the photo on Sanction, it is 0216-4735 -- 4735 or 4785.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: 4735, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 4735, yeah. I think he can then confirm to us whether he is actually sure about the recognition of this person, Cop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same with both pictures. I cannot be 100 per cent sure it's Cop but I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And since we are talking about percentages, I may as well ask you, sir, if you had to place a percentage on your certainty, what would it be that this is Cop?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could move along and just flip that photograph over, please, sir? Do you recognise anyone in this photograph? And this is 0216-4737.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a colleague from Milici, whose name I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say he's a colleague from Milici, is he a 1st Company PJP officer, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say he's from Milici, do you mean that he is also a police officer from Milici?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He belonged to the Milici police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just for the record you're identifying the man with an automatic rifle over his shoulder; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could flip over the next photograph, to the next photograph, please? This is 0216-4738. Do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left, that's another colleague of mine from the 1st Company. He was from the Skelani station. I don't know his name. He was called by the nickname Dugi. And that's his brother with the same nickname, Dugi. He belonged to the Special Police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just flip that over, please? And we'll move to the next photograph. This is 0216-4742. Do you recognise the area that is depicted in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with any certainty, but the likelihood is high that this is the Sandici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let's move to the next photograph. And let's move to the next photograph over that, sir. 0216-4757. Do you recognise the individual with the black headband, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a member of the 1st Company, a policeman from Skelani. I think his last name is Vasic. I don't know about the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to the next photograph. We can save sometime and move along to the next photograph after that, sir. This is 0216-4759. Do you recognise this individual, sir? 4760.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a member of the 1st Company and worked at the police station in Zvornik. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you could just turn that photograph over please, sir and read the number on the back, make sure the record is clear?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, please, just read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We are looking at 0216-4771. Do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a policeman called Krstic, member of the 1st Company, from the Milici police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you're indicating the individual to the most right on the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the right, next to the civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Moving along, if you would flip to the next photograph, please? This is 0216-4772. Do you recognise anyone in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they are also members of the 1st Company from the Milici police station. I don't know their names or nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And these are the individuals on either side of the man in the foreground in the light-coloured shirt, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could flip to the next photograph, please? 0216-4780.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a policeman from Zvornik, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was he also a 1st Company PJP member, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is this the man in the mustache to the right of the image?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If you would flip the photograph, please? 0216-4784. Do you recognise this individual?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a member of the 1st Company, who was from the Vlasenica police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just flip that over, please, that photograph? This is 0216-4877. Do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know both of them. The one above, with the sunglasses and a cigarette, is Goran Zekic. And the other one is Milosavljevic. His nickname was Giga, but I'm not sure about the first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how is it that you recognise or know these two individuals, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see them every day or almost every day in Srebrenica and I know them quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know what military unit they belonged to at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they belonged to the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. And just flip the photograph over, please. This is 0216-4878. Do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know this man smoking a cigarette. That's Milomir Tanasijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: There appear to be a couple of men with cigarettes. Are you describing the man who is directly facing the camera, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how is it that you know this individual?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a neighbour of mine. We live in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know what unit he was serving in at the time of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was also in the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I may have neglected to ask you this earlier. The individual that you identified as Like Milinkovic, do you know what military or army unit he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how should I put it? He switched units. I'm not sure. He was in the Panthers unit and then he was in the Bratunac Brigade. I'm not sure at the time when these photographs were taken whether he was in the Panthers at that time or in the Bratunac Brigade, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How about Mr. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tomic, the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may have P02478 on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see an image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please take a couple of moments to orient yourself. I know you looked at this with me during your proofing but it was a little bigger so if you need a couple of seconds to take a good, hard look at it, familiarise yourself with it, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If you would take the pen that's attached to your computer with the assistance of Madam Usher, I'm going to ask you to mark first of all the route that you took as you entered Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the main road here. [Marks] Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you just turn that into an arrow, I think that will be sufficient, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] I can't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown and identified yourself in a photograph earlier speaking to a woman. Would you just mark with a circle where that location was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please mark with an X the area which you identified as the orchard where you say you spent some time that day on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. If you would just write your initials on the lower left-hand -- right-hand corner and today's date, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we can save it once you're done. And then we'll move on to the last exhibit, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as soon as it's saved if we could have P02103, please? And that's page 40. If we can zoom in a little, please? That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want you to just take a couple moments and orient yourself.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's okay. It's okay. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you described a location where you were posted on the evening of 12 July, prior to the explosion that you heard. Can you just mark that location with a number 1, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. The location where I was before the explosion or when the explosion occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You've indicated with an X. Now, you described moving to an abandoned house immediately after that. Can you just mark that area with a number 1, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's this house or that house, but that would be, I think, this one here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You also testified about another destroyed house that you saw when you moved your position the next morning. Can you just write a number 2 next to that house, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you mark with a number 3 the area which you described as a meadow where you saw the prisoners heading that same morning?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say a number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If you would just place your initials in the lower right-hand corner and today's date, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can save it now and we'll be done with this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has put July instead of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, as my colleagues know, you were interviewed by the OTP, by the RS commission in, I think, 2004, and more recently by the authorities in Sarajevo, just a couple of weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever ask you for a report? For example, did Mr. Pantic ever ask you for a report concerning the actions of you or your company in Potocari or along the road in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You mean from me personally? Did he ask for any report?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never reported -- wrote any reports about any combat activities, and I really don't know if anyone actually did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, did anyone ever ask you? Did Mr. Pantic ever ask you for a report, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any 1st Company PJP members ever disciplined by the RS MUP in connection with their deployment to Potocari and that road segment in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of any investigation ever being initiated by the RS MUP concerning the deployment of the PJP units or the Special Police Brigade units to those areas in July 1995? I'm not talking about the RS commission.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir. I thank you for your time. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is going first? We need about three minutes at the end for our decision. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic? Could you kindly introduce yourself with the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Your Honours. Before I introduce myself to the witness, I would like to ask for one thing. We indicated we would need one hour to ask this witness, but in light of the examination-in-chief today, I would like to consult my client for just one minute. I believe that our examination might be substantially shorter. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Stojanovic. And if you want to consult him in private, I think that can be arranged, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanojevic, my name is Miodrag Stojanovic and I'm here representing Mr. Borovcanin, as his Defence counsel, and I believe that we will be able to go through your cross-examination fairly quickly. Would you agree with me that in July 1995, at the level of the public security centre in Zvornik, that a total of six companies of the PJP were set up and they were, in fact, a PJP Battalion, they formed a PJP battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This PJP battalion was under the command of the Zvornik public security centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And this battalion comprised your company, the 1st PJP company, which I would posit was composed of mostly younger police officers from the police stations that were part of the Zvornik public security centre; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, in July 1995, to the best of your knowledge, how many people were there in the 1st PJP company?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe about 60 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And they were divided into three platoons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You described how and why you were engaged in action, and I wanted to ask you if at times you went to different areas and sometimes even with the Special Police Brigade units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We often went into the field together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In those joint combat groups, if I may call them that, the commander of such a combat group would be somebody from the Special Police Brigade; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to move on to your activities in July. You said that on the 12th of July, in the morning, you were tasked with going to an area in front of the Yellow Bridge and UN check-point from the direction of Bratunac, that would be to the right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To search the terrain in the direction of the village of Gornji Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You described the death of a mine layer, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that this mine layer, who was a member of the Bratunac Brigade, that he was killed as he was trying to open the passage through the minefield that you were supposed to use on your way to search the terrain; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you by any chance know the name of this mine layer or bomb disposal person who died that morning?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know his name. I knew him by sight. I think he was from Sase but I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that during the search of this terrain, to the right of the road, you did not encounter any troops of the BH army or any civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any specific orders as to what to do if you encountered any civilians?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't get any orders, but there were commanders there with us and we could ask them about any procedure that we were to apply if we encountered anyone. But we didn't encounter any troops or any civilians until we arrived at the UN base, which is where we encountered the first civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if you had any specific tasks regarding the disarming of the United Nations troops or any attacks on to the UN check-point at Yellow Bridge?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure that we didn't have any such tasks because my unit did not take part in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long did it take you to carry out this task, to search the terrain, before you came back to this road leading to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly but it may have been an hour or two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right if I said that you practically went all the way down to the road at around 9.00 or between 9.00 and 10.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be specific but I think that this would be the approximate time because I can't really orient myself in time. I can't confirm that for you with 100 per cent certainty, but it's possible, you may be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You know this area well, I conclude that on the basis of your ability to recognise things?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, this is where I was born and I do know it quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, your village, Zalazje, is maybe about five kilometres away from the UN base, am I correct in stating that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe even a little bit less than five kilometres but that would be the approximate distance, five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you when the war broke out? Were you in Srebrenica or in the village?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Srebrenica, in my apartment, and then under pressure we were forced to leave Srebrenica and I went to my village. I stayed there for a while. I saw that it was not safe. And I went to Bratunac while my relatives and my friends, my neighbours, remained in the village until it was attacked by the Muslim units and burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, until the 15th of July 1995, you actually were not able to see your home, your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was not able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like, Your Honours, perhaps this is a good time for us to go back to Sanction, to revisit photograph ERN number 0216-4862. I would like to ask one more question about this photograph because I think that my learned colleague, Mr. Thayer, really did ask all the proper questions but while we are waiting for this photograph, Mr. Stanojevic, you told us that you were able to recognise quite a few units and formations of the army in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were able to recognise some elements of the Bratunac Brigade in Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this your last question, Mr. Stojanovic? Or do you have further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will just ask one more question about this photograph and I would be done with the questions for today, and we may have another 15 minutes at the most. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go through this photo quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanojevic, my last question for today is you were able to recognise these two men on these photographs, you told us their last names?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, in July 1995, which unit did these two men belong to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were soldiers of the Bratunac Brigade. I don't know their battalion but I do know that they were soldiers of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I will not have any more questions for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stanojevic, we'll continue tomorrow in the afternoon and in the meantime between today and tomorrow do not allow anyone to discuss with you the subject matter of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, number 1, tomorrow, we are just putting you on notice so that you will be able to regulate your evidence accordingly, tomorrow, we'll need to finish early. And that will be between 6 and 6.15 in the afternoon. All right? So you are given advance notice of that. Now we come to the decision that we promised you. This is the decision that we have arising out of the issue raised by Mr. Bourgon. At issue is -- and others -- is whether the testimony of Witness PW-128 should be postponed in the light of new information provided by him during his proofing session on Sunday of this week, a few days before his scheduled testimony. Because of the objection of counsel for the Defence of Mr. Nikolic, the Trial Chamber has decided not to have regard to the relevant document sheet, which purportedly describes the new information provided. It is almost inevitable, and this will, we feel we need to drive home, that in the course of a trial, especially a lengthy one like this one, a witness may disclose new information in some instances, even in the course of his or her testimony. This, in and of itself, however does not justify postponement of that testimony. Additional investigations may of course become necessary, may take place, and further questions may well be justified as a result of new information gathered. However, these can be addressed by recalling the witness at a later date, while still allowing his or her direct examination and cross-examination to proceed as scheduled. We believe this to be the proper course of action in relation to PW-128 and we therefore are denying the motion for postponement with the understanding that any of the Defence teams can make an application later on to recall this particular witness, if this becomes necessary. We would, however, like to highlight one further issue. The Trial Chamber is concerned by the time being lost on submissions as to whether prior statements and proofing notes should be available to it, in particular instances. More disquieting is the belief that some of you have indicated you have that whether the Trial Chamber has access or not to such documents depends on your consent or permission. All this arises because, differently from other Trial Chambers, this Chamber has taken a somewhat unique position not to receive such material generally. We are, however, actively considering what steps would be best to take in the interests of justice which would also avoid unnecessary consumption of time in proceedings. We stand adjourned until tomorrow at 2.15.
